newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bus company settles over fired veggie driver.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bus company settles over fired veggie driver.

text.p: A California bus company has agreed to pay $50,000 to settle a suit brought by a vegetarian bus driver fired for refusing to hand out hamburger coupons to passengers, his lawyer said on Tuesday.

Bruce Anderson had filed a discrimination charge with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and followed that up in June with a lawsuit against his former employer, the Orange County Transit Authority.

Anderson, 38, is a vegan who eats no meat, dairy product, eggs or any other food deriving from animals. He does not wear leather or use any products such as soap or toothpaste that contain animal products or that are tested on animals.
He was fired by OCTA in May after he refused to hand out the hamburger coupons to passengers as part of a promotion between the transit company and a local fast-food chain.

His lawyer, Gloria Allred, said his dismissal violated his civil rights by discriminating against Anderson on the basis of his religious views and also violated his constitutional right to freedom of speech.

The company, based in the Orange County suburbs south of Los Angeles, had refused to compromise by giving Anderson desk work during the burger campaign or to accept his offer to put the coupons in a box for passengers to take, Allred said.
She said that in addition to paying Anderson $50,000, the company had agreed to modify its employee handbook to conform with EEOC guidelines.
Anderson, who had worked for OCTA for five years, has declined to return to work there and has moved to northern California.
At a news conference on Tuesday, he said: "The slaughtering of animals has got to stop -- this is just a beginning, I guess."
